criterion: OTP abuse/risk/recovery design; record unresolved choices and no production writes.

unresolved.proposal: Bounded sessions per FR-038 and D-053: short-lived access token (proposed 600 seconds), rotating refresh with reuse detection and finite idle/absolute lifetime (proposed idle 30 days, absolute 90 days), silent rotating refresh within those bounds to satisfy FR-004/FR-005 and SC-002 without weakening the R2 revocation boundary. Lifetime is enforced server-side, never client-controlled. Long-inactive or risky access is not refreshed silently; it requires independent previously verified email (FR-038/D-053) and fails closed into assisted recovery when proof is absent. Local/dev values are documented separately from deployed values; exact production durations remain for Security + Product ratification.
unresolved.remainingEvidence: Exact access/idle/absolute durations, refresh reuse-detection grace and rotation behavior are not yet ratified against native (004) client behavior and the 500-active-user target; ratification needs a completed G-SESSION ADR approved by Security + Product, isolated fixtures proving server lifetime enforcement against the real Supabase session model (R2), and a decision on whether refresh rotation preserves or invalidates other device sessions before T032.

unresolved.proposal: Reconcile the 001 device list with 004 single-active-session per G-SESSION: multiple revocable devices per account, each a bounded session, with owner-scoped server-only listing (FR-040, R3) and device labels derived from user_agent (T030). Targeted and bulk revoke share the same independent proof (FR-040; risk.singleAndBulkRevokeSameProof). Use an app-level revocation record consulted on every authorization and renewed-token path, never signOut(session_id) and never an OTP-only risky fallback (R3). The device-count UX conflict with 004 remains explicitly unratified (spec.md).
unresolved.remainingEvidence: Reconciliation of 001 multiple revocable devices versus 004 single active session, plus the maximum concurrent device count and oldest-session eviction policy, are unratified; ratification needs a tested supported targeted-revocation mechanism with isolated tests proving an old JWT is denied on every domain and direct path before T031, and a UX decision on device-count limits.

unresolved.proposal: Define concrete risk signals per D-053, FR-001 and FR-005: new device, changed number, missing/expired session, long inactivity beyond the idle limit, repeated failed OTP verification and device/session anomaly. On any signal, phone OTP alone never unlocks historical data (risk.phoneOtpAloneUnlocksHistory=false); the account must supply independent previously verified email proof that is account-and-action bound and single-use (FR-038/D-053), otherwise fail closed into assisted recovery. Normal same-device returns avoid SMS (FR-005/SC-002) without re-triggering risk.
unresolved.remainingEvidence: Precise risk-signal taxonomy, thresholds (inactivity duration, failed-attempt count, anomaly heuristics) and which signals are sticky versus transient are unratified; ratification needs Security + Product approval and isolated fixtures showing a newly verified risky device cannot read prior history without independent proof, and that unavailable validation denies (risk.unavailableValidationDenies).

unresolved.proposal: When both factors are lost, recovery resolves to audited assistance without automatic unlock per FR-041/D-053: a staff-assisted, audit-recorded procedure that does not auto-unlock history or transfer identity. It must collect independent evidence (identity document plus ownership corroboration) recorded in staff_actions, never delivery facts, address, plan or last delivery (spec Recovery and ownership; D-053). Support approval alone is insufficient (recovery.supportApprovalAloneSufficient=false); a factor is never replaced using only that same factor.
unresolved.remainingEvidence: Concrete assisted-recovery evidence checklist (which identity/ownership documents, verification steps, mandatory second reviewer or founder sign-off, retention duration) and its pass/fail criteria are unratified; ratification needs a G-RECOVERY ADR approved by Security + Support defining evidence thresholds, audit fields and proof that support approval alone never unlocks history, before risky-history access launches.

unresolved.proposal: Live OTP/WhatsApp/email suppliers, secret-manager credentials, templates, consent and failure runbooks are unresolved per G-PROVIDERS. Server-side Send-SMS hook worker credentials, supplier deliverability/cost, hook timeout/error behavior and cross-instance spend/quota protection require qualification (R4). Quota is checked before send with shared atomic reservation, idempotency, no blind retry and bounded verification attempts (otp.*). Provider selection is not a configuration-only change; providerQualified stays false until live qualification.
unresolved.remainingEvidence: Supplier selection, credentials in a secret manager, template/consent wording, failure runbooks and an approved per-task/project OTP spend ceiling with billing reconciliation (G-BUDGET) are unratified; ratification needs founder + operations sign-off and a live non-production qualification proving quota-before-send, atomic accounting, idempotency and cost metering against the chosen provider before any production send is authorized.
